newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO END CO-OP BANK SECTOR REFORM IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO END CO-OP BANK SECTOR REFORM IN 1997.

text.p: The long process of restructuring Poland's ailing co-operative banking sector should end this year with the creation of a new three-tier system of banks, the agriculture minister said on Wednesday.
"The construction of a three-level system of co-operative, regional and nationwide banks should be completed this year," Roman Jagielinski told a news conference.

Jagielinski said that the last two of nine regional banks, which would form a group with small co-operative banks and be guided by nationwide bank Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ), would be created in the near future.
BGZ groups 1,200 of the country's 1,600 small cooperative banks.
Before the scheme started two years ago nearly one-third of the country's cooperative banks were in danger of bankruptcy after a huge wave of bad loans to farmers in the early 1990s.
